html:
A fortress built by the Dutch East India Company at Anping, in today's Tainan, on the southwest coast of Taiwan. Work went on from 1624 to 1634.

The Dutch had tried to trade with China from the Penghu islands, and the Ming pushed them off to Taiwan, then outside Chinese rule. From Zeelandia the company governed Dutch Formosa for 38 years. It ran a trading post for Chinese silk, sugar and Japanese silver, taxed deer hides and brought in Chinese farmers from Fujian to grow rice and sugar cane. The company's records from the fort are the first long written history of Taiwan.

In 1661 the Ming loyalist Koxinga landed with a large fleet and besieged the fort for nine months. The Dutch surrendered in early 1662, and Koxinga made Taiwan his base against the Qing. See Koxinga settles Taiwan. Only some brick walls of the fort survive.
